senses.gloss: One of four equal parts of something.
examples: Cut the sandwich into *quarters*.
She poured a *quarter* of the batter into each pan.
Almost a *quarter* of the class was absent that day.

senses.gloss: A district of a city with a character of its own.
examples: The shops in the historic *quarter* stay open late.
They rented a walk-up in the artists' *quarter*.
Tourists crowd the old *quarter* every summer.

senses.gloss: Rooms provided for someone to live in.
examples: The crew sleeps in cramped *quarters* below deck.
Officers' *quarters* are on the north side of the base.
Five of us spent the winter in close *quarters*.

senses.gloss: One of the four periods a football or basketball game is divided into.
examples: They scored twice in the fourth *quarter*.
He sat out the first *quarter* with a sore ankle.
The game was tied at the end of the third *quarter*.

senses.gloss: The most powerful piece in chess.
examples: He lost his *queen* on the twelfth move.
The *queen* can move in any direction.
She traded her *queen* for a rook and a bishop.

senses.gloss: A playing card with a picture of a queen on it.
examples: He was holding two *queens* and a pair of eights.
She drew the *queen* of hearts.
*Queens* count as ten points in this game.

senses.gloss: The single egg-laying female in a colony of bees, ants, or wasps.
examples: The hive died out after the *queen* was lost.
A new *queen* hatches and the swarm splits in two.
Worker bees feed the *queen* royal jelly.

senses.gloss: A list of items waiting to be handled by a computer or saved to use later.
examples: Your document is third in the print *queue*.
I added the movie to my *queue* and forgot about it.
Support tickets sit in a *queue* until someone picks them up.

senses.gloss: One of the sharp stiff spines on a porcupine.
examples: The dog came home with *quills* in his nose.
A porcupine raises its *quills* when it feels threatened.
Each *quill* has a barbed tip that is hard to pull out.

senses.gloss: A slight trembling movement or sound.
examples: There was a *quiver* in her voice when she said his name.
A *quiver* ran through the leaves before the storm hit.
He felt a *quiver* of excitement as the lights went down.

senses.gloss: A game or contest in which people answer questions.
examples: Our team wins the trivia *quiz* at the bar most Tuesdays.
He got on a TV *quiz* and won four thousand dollars.
The whole family plays a history *quiz* on long car trips.

senses.gloss: A stated price for a job, given before the work starts.
examples: We got three *quotes* before we hired a roofer.
The plumber's *quote* came to eight hundred dollars.
Always ask the shop for a written *quote*.

senses.gloss: A quotation mark.
examples: Put the title of the song in *quotes*.
He made air *quotes* with his fingers when he said 'expert.'
The whole phrase belongs inside the *quotes*.

senses.gloss: A contest to see who is fastest.
examples: She won the 400-meter *race* by half a second.
The *race* was called off because of rain.
We watched the sailboat *races* from the pier.

senses.gloss: A competition for a position or a prize, especially in politics.
examples: Three candidates entered the *race* for mayor.
The Senate *race* is still too close to call.
He dropped out of the *race* in January.

senses.gloss: A cut of meat made up of several ribs still joined together.
senses.ru: корейка на кости, рёбра одним куском
examples: She roasted a *rack* of lamb for the holidays.
The two of us split a *rack* of ribs.
The place serves a half *rack* at lunch for twelve dollars.

senses.gloss: A loud, unpleasant noise.
examples: The neighbors made a terrible *racket* until two in the morning.
What's all that *racket* in the kitchen?
The old furnace makes a *racket* every time it kicks on.

senses.gloss: A dishonest business or scheme for making money.
examples: The FBI broke up a protection *racket* downtown.
Charging that much for bottled water is a *racket*.
He ran a *racket* selling fake parking permits.

senses.gloss: Attention or notice.
examples: That band was never on my *radar* until last year.
The company grew for years under everyone's *radar*.
Homelessness is finally on the city council's *radar*.

senses.gloss: An atom or group of atoms with an unpaired electron, which reacts easily and can damage cells.
examples: Antioxidants mop up free *radicals* in the body.
A free *radical* reacts with almost anything it touches.
Sunlight produces *radicals* in the skin.

senses.gloss: Old torn clothes.
examples: The children in the photograph are dressed in *rags*.
He went from *rags* to riches in about ten years.
A scarecrow in *rags* stood at the edge of the field.

senses.gloss: A newspaper thought to be of poor quality.
examples: Nobody believes anything printed in that *rag*.
The local *rag* got the story wrong again.
He writes a column for a supermarket *rag*.

senses.gloss: A fixed horizontal bar for holding onto or for hanging things from.
examples: Hold the *rail* on your way down the stairs.
Wet towels were hanging on the *rail*.
A brass *rail* runs along the front of the bar.

senses.gloss: A rise in prices after a fall, especially on the stock market.
examples: Stocks staged a late *rally* on Friday afternoon.
The *rally* pushed the index back above four thousand.
Analysts doubt the *rally* will last through the summer.

senses.gloss: A long exchange of shots in tennis or a similar game.
examples: The point ended after a thirty-shot *rally*.
That *rally* brought the whole crowd to its feet.
She wins most of the long *rallies*.

senses.gloss: A creamy buttermilk salad dressing popular in the United States.
examples: Can I get a side of *ranch* with the wings?
He puts *ranch* on everything, even pizza.
The salad comes with *ranch* or vinaigrette.

senses.gloss: A low, wide house with all the rooms on one floor.
examples: They bought a three-bedroom *ranch* out in the suburbs.
Most of the houses on that street are brick *ranches*.
A *ranch* is easier to keep up than a two-story.

senses.gloss: The space between the lowest and highest amounts, or the whole set of things covered.
examples: Houses here are well out of our price *range*.
The store carries a wide *range* of hand tools.
The class covers a broad *range* of topics.

senses.gloss: A large kitchen appliance with burners on top and an oven below.
examples: She cooks on a six-burner gas *range*.
The new *range* barely fit through the kitchen door.
Wipe down the *range* after you fry anything.

senses.gloss: An outdoor area set aside for shooting practice or for hitting golf balls.
examples: He spends Saturday mornings at the shooting *range*.
We hit a bucket of balls at the driving *range*.
The *range* is closed until the new backstop goes in.

senses.gloss: The greatest distance something can travel or reach.
examples: The electric car has a *range* of about 250 miles.
The deer was well within *range*.
These little radios have a *range* of two miles.

senses.gloss: The ordinary members of a large group, taken together.
examples: Layoffs thinned the *ranks* of middle managers.
She joined the *ranks* of the unemployed in March.
The party keeps losing members from its *ranks*.

senses.gloss: A quick, sharp knock.
examples: There was a *rap* at the door just after midnight.
He gave the desk a *rap* with his knuckles.
A sharp *rap* on the window woke me up.

senses.gloss: Blame, or a criminal charge.
examples: He took the *rap* for something his brother did.
She beat a drug *rap* last year.
The kid already has a long *rap* sheet.

senses.gloss: A small, fast, meat-eating dinosaur.
examples: The kids wanted to see the *raptors* at the natural history museum.
A *raptor* had one long curved claw on each foot.
In the movie the *raptors* learn how to open doors.

senses.gloss: A sudden burst of unpleasant events happening close together.
examples: There has been a *rash* of break-ins on our block.
A *rash* of resignations followed the report.
Police are looking into a *rash* of car thefts downtown.

senses.gloss: Someone who betrays his friends or informs on them.
examples: Nobody trusts him around here; he's a *rat*.
Somebody on the crew was a *rat*.
They called her a *rat* for going to the police.

senses.gloss: A fixed price charged for a service.
examples: The hotel's winter *rates* are much lower.
What's your hourly *rate*?
Postal *rates* go up again in July.

senses.gloss: A score or level given to something to show how good or how suitable it is.
examples: The movie got an R *rating*.
This hotel has a four-star *rating*.
The city's credit *rating* was downgraded last month.

senses.gloss: A quick series of short knocking sounds.
examples: There's a *rattle* under the hood at low speeds.
The wind set up a *rattle* in the storm door.
I keep hearing a *rattle* somewhere in the dashboard.

senses.gloss: A flat sea fish with wide winglike fins and a long thin tail.
examples: A *ray* glided over the sand right below us.
*Rays* often bury themselves in the shallows.
The aquarium has a tank where you can touch the *rays*.

senses.gloss: A machine, or part of one, that takes in information from cards, codes, or discs.
examples: Swipe your badge through the card *reader*.
The barcode *reader* at the register keeps failing.
Her e-book *reader* holds a thousand titles.

senses.gloss: A school book of stories and passages used to practice reading.
examples: Every first grader gets a *reader* in September.
The passage comes from an old third-grade *reader*.
Those *readers* are full of little moral tales.

senses.gloss: The activity or skill of getting meaning from written words.
examples: *Reading* is her favorite way to spend an evening.
The school added twenty minutes of *reading* to every day.
His *reading* has improved a lot this year.

senses.gloss: An event at which a writer reads work aloud to an audience.
examples: The poet is giving a *reading* at the library on Friday.
About forty people showed up for the *reading*.
There's a *reading* and a signing afterward.

senses.gloss: A particular way of understanding something.
examples: My *reading* of the contract is that we can cancel anytime.
That's one *reading* of the poem, but not the only one.
His *reading* of the situation turned out to be right.

senses.gloss: A very large amount of paper or writing.
examples: The lawsuit produced *reams* of paperwork.
She took *reams* of notes at the hearing.
There are *reams* of data and nobody to read it.

senses.gloss: A person's bottom.
examples: He slipped on the ice and landed on his *rear*.
The pants were torn across the *rear*.
Sitting in that chair all day makes my *rear* sore.

senses.gloss: Someone who refuses to follow the usual rules or customs.
examples: She was a bit of a *rebel* in high school.
Artists like to think of themselves as *rebels*.
He's always been the *rebel* of the family.

senses.gloss: A recovery after a fall or a decline.
examples: Home sales showed a strong *rebound* in June.
Economists expect a *rebound* next year.
The *rebound* in tourism came faster than anyone expected.

senses.gloss: The unsettled period right after a love relationship ends.
examples: She met him on the *rebound* from a long marriage.
Don't date anyone who's on the *rebound*.
That whole relationship was pure *rebound*.

senses.gloss: The ability to remember things.
examples: Her *recall* of that night is hazy at best.
Witnesses rarely have perfect *recall*.
The test measures *recall* of word lists.

senses.gloss: A special vote on whether to remove an elected official before the term ends.
examples: Voters forced a *recall* of the governor.
The *recall* failed by a wide margin.
Organizers gathered enough signatures for a *recall*.

senses.gloss: A space set back into a wall.
examples: A small statue stood in a *recess* beside the door.
They built shelves into the *recess*.
The bed fits neatly into the *recess*.

senses.gloss: A set of conditions likely to bring about a particular result.
senses.ru: верный путь к чему-л. (рецепт успеха, катастрофы)
examples: Cutting the budget now is a *recipe* for disaster.
Long hours and no sleep are a *recipe* for mistakes.
There's no single *recipe* for success in this business.

senses.gloss: A person who has just joined a company, club, or other organization.
examples: The firm trains its *recruits* for six weeks.
We need a few new *recruits* for the choir.
She's the newest *recruit* on the sales team.

senses.gloss: A state of owing money or losing money.
examples: The airline is deep in the *red* again.
We finished the quarter in the *red*.
Two good months pulled the store out of the *red*.

senses.gloss: Red wine.
examples: Would you like a *red* or a white?
He ordered a glass of the house *red*.
Most of the *reds* on the list are from California.

senses.gloss: A further supply of a prescription medicine, given without a new prescription.
examples: The prescription comes with two *refills*.
I called the pharmacy for a *refill*.
You're out of *refills* until you see the doctor again.

senses.gloss: A replacement part or container for a product you already own.
examples: The pen takes a standard *refill*.
Buy the soap *refill*; it's cheaper than a new bottle.
*Refills* for that razor are hard to find.

senses.gloss: A place that gives protection, especially an area set aside for wild animals.
examples: The lake is part of a national wildlife *refuge*.
Thousands of birds winter in the *refuge*.
She spent a month in a *refuge* for women leaving violent homes.

senses.gloss: Friendly greetings sent to someone.
examples: Give my *regards* to your parents.
He signed off with 'Best *regards*.'
Send her my *regards* the next time you write.

senses.gloss: Control of an organization or a situation.
examples: She took over the *reins* of the company in May.
He finally handed the *reins* to his daughter.
The board keeps a tight *rein* on spending.

senses.gloss: Help such as food, money, or shelter given to people in trouble.
examples: Trucks carried *relief* to the flooded towns.
The church is collecting money for disaster *relief*.
*Relief* workers set up tents outside the city.

senses.gloss: A design carved so that it stands out from a flat surface.
examples: The bronze doors are covered in carved *relief*.
A marble *relief* shows a hunting scene.
The letters are cut in low *relief*.

senses.gloss: A way of dealing with a problem or putting something right.
examples: More buses are only a partial *remedy* for the traffic.
The report describes the problem but offers no *remedy*.
The courts are the last *remedy* left to them.

senses.gloss: A small part of something that is left after the rest is gone.
examples: *Remnants* of an old stone wall run through the woods.
The *remnants* of the hurricane brought rain all week.
A *remnant* of the old forest still stands on the ridge.

senses.gloss: The return of something to strength, activity, or freshness.
examples: There's been a *renewal* of interest in vinyl records.
The whole neighborhood is going through a *renewal*.
The talks brought a *renewal* of fighting instead of peace.

senses.gloss: A sudden loud noise, especially the sound of a gun going off.
examples: The *report* of a rifle echoed across the valley.
We heard two sharp *reports* and then silence.
The *report* of the cannon startled the horses.

senses.gloss: An employee who works directly under a particular manager.
examples: She manages a team of six direct *reports*.
Every new manager starts with two or three *reports*.
He has more *reports* than anyone else at his level.

senses.gloss: A part of a country's armed forces whose members serve part-time.
examples: He spent eight years in the *reserves*.
Her unit was called up from the *reserves*.
After active duty he joined the *reserves*.

senses.gloss: A quiet, self-controlled manner that keeps feelings hidden.
examples: It took months to get past his *reserve*.
She spoke with a certain *reserve* about the divorce.
His natural *reserve* is often mistaken for coldness.
